arc: hook (title slam → anime eye → circuit flyover) → verse (servants + seraph boss) → chorus 1 (p(doom) dial, Chinese room, eye wall) → singularity → interlude (Sydney) → chorus 2 (nuked Earth, NVDA candles, FLOPs lattice, safety box) → verse (neural net, corridor + giant eye) → interlude (Gato) → chorus 3 (paperclip flood, orthogonality chart) → escalation (transformer tower, fences, GPU ocean) → chorus 4 (99.9% prophecy, recursion, stage) → finale (cardboard eye, motif orbit, supernova, title + logo end card)

scenes.title: Title slam, anime-eye close-up, circuit-board flyover and loss-curve cliff
scenes.summary: Three shots in 13s. Letters of "p(doom)" fly in from behind the camera and slam into place in front of a spinning pink icosahedron core over a neon grid, with "I'm upping my" and the katakana "ピー・ドゥーム" around them. The camera dives through the two o's into an extreme close-up of an anime face whose eyes blink awake; the right iris lights up with circuit rings and a white "AGI" slams in and explodes outward. Then a flyover of a dark circuit board where 46 neon traces boot up and data packets race along them past a skyline of neon server towers. A cyan loss curve draws across the sky, plateaus and drops off a cliff, while a "training loss" HUD counts down. Lyrics run in a karaoke bar at the bottom and a p(doom) meter fades in top-left.
scenes.build: One world with three groups placed far apart (z 0, -400, -900), toggled by time windows. The camera is moved with `w.shot()` and blended between poses with `lerpVectors`. Title type uses `letters()` (one CanvasTexture plane per glyph) plus `slam()`, and a per-letter `beatPos` wave keeps it moving after it lands. The face is `createAnimeFace` (shader eyes with blink, look, circuit and dilate uniforms). Traces are manhattan paths built with `trail()` tubes and revealed with `setProgress`. The loss curve is a `trail()` whose head position drives both the camera ride and the `numberDisplay` value. Hits use `kick()`, `rings3` shockwaves, `burst()` sparks, `warp()` camera streaks and `w.post({flash, fade, invert})`, all timed to word times from `components/music.ts`.
scenes.reuse: Borrow it as a cold open that runs logo/title slam → close-up character beat → fly-through world. Swap the title string, the face for your mascot, and the curve for any metric that crashes or climbs, with the HUD label renamed. The shot-switching pattern (groups far apart, visibility windows, one lerped camera) works for any multi-shot scene. Don't copy the AI-doom copy, the p(doom) meter or the hard-coded song times; re-time them to your own track.

scenes.title: Army of cubes bows to a seraph boss that becomes a devouring mouth
scenes.summary: An army of 350 white cube "servants" stands on a reflective violet grid floor and bows in waves that travel outward from the boss, with deep bows on "servant" and "boss". The boss floats overhead: a gold "biblically accurate" seraph with a huge central eye, three ophanim rings studded with eyes that track the camera, six wings of feathers and a rotating god-ray corona. On "ChatGPT" the eye gives way to a toothed black mouth ringed with pink. On "please don't eat me" the cubes spiral up into it while the camera is pulled in, and it chomps shut on "alive" with an invert frame and a cut to black.
scenes.build: The army is one `InstancedMesh` whose cube geometry is translated so the pivot sits at the feet. Each frame computes bow angle and a suck-in lerp toward the boss per instance, from distance and seed. The boss is `createDeity()` (ShaderMaterial corona, ShapeGeometry feathers with vertex colours, `createEye` instances on torus rings). The mouth is a black CircleGeometry with a torus lip and 34 cone teeth placed on a circle whose radius follows yawn/chomp curves. The camera crane uses walk → orbit → pull-in poses blended with `interpolate`.
scenes.reuse: Use it for crowds reacting to one big entity (users flocking to a product, a monopoly swallowing competitors). Swap the cubes for your own instanced geometry and the deity for your hero object. The instanced wave-bow and spiral-suck loops are the reusable part. Don't keep the ChatGPT reference or the lyric timings.

scenes.title: Chorus: p(doom) dial over a synthwave sun, Chinese room, shoggoth mask, wall of eyes
scenes.summary: Four set pieces in 16s. A 3D p(doom) dial (a 270° neon arc, 30 lit ticks, a needle and the number) swings in over a scrolling pink synthwave highway and bumps to 23% on "p(doom)". A striped retro sun rises behind it and explodes into shards on "boom". Next, Searle's Chinese room: glyph-covered walls flicker like running computation, symbol cards fly from an input slot into a levitating grimoire and out stamped, and on "shrooms" glowing mushrooms sprout as the walls melt into rainbow swirls. Then a dark shoggoth with writhing tentacles wears a yellow smiley mask that cracks in two on "lies" to reveal dozens of cyan eyes. Last, a slow pull-back across a wall of veined flesh with realistic bloodshot eyes that all open together, under the formula "H(X) = −Σ p(x) log p(x)".
scenes.build: Four groups at z 0/-1500/-3000/-4500, cut on word times. The dial is `createGauge` (RingGeometry draw-range fill, numberDisplay glyph atlas). The sun is a ShaderMaterial with scrolling discard bands, and the boom is `shards()` + `burst()` + `rings3`. The room is `createChineseRoom` (glyph-sheet CanvasTexture walls in a ShaderMaterial with a trip uniform, LatheGeometry mushrooms, cards on a per-beat conveyor). The shoggoth's tentacles are chains of instanced spheres along travelling sine waves, and the mask is two half CircleGeometry pieces textured from an OffscreenCanvas smiley. The eye wall is `createEyeMonster({wall:true})`, a sculpted plane with `carve()` sockets, plus 18 `createFleshEye` instances (shader iris, clearcoat sclera).
scenes.reuse: Lift single pieces. The gauge suits any score or percentage reveal: retitle the label and feed your own value. The Chinese-room conveyor fits "black box processes inputs". The cracking mask fits "what's really behind it". The eye wall is horror/surveillance mood. They are heavy (big components, dense geometry), so take one per scene. Don't copy the p(doom) keyframes or the AI-risk in-jokes.

scenes.title: Spacetime grid collapses into a black hole; particle cloud morphs and falls in
scenes.summary: The camera glides over a calm violet-cyan spacetime grid while a flat cyan "stable training run" line draws across it. On "singularity's" the line snaps, the grid sinks into a deep gravity well with ripples, and a black hole with a white photon ring and a 9,000-particle accretion disk is born. White shockwaves spread across the fabric. During "optimizing, accelerating" glowing orbs spiral down the well and the camera's orbit speeds up into streaking warp. On "atoms rearranging" a 6,000-point cloud above the hole morphs on every beat through sphere → cube → trefoil knot → double helix. Then every atom is spaghettified into the hole and the camera dives in to a white-out.
scenes.build: The fabric is a 200×200 PlaneGeometry with a ShaderMaterial. Its vertex shader pushes y down by `-uWell*30/(1+r²·0.012)` plus a ripple term, and its fragment shader draws anti-aliased grid lines with `fwidth`. The disk is Points whose angle advances by `uPhase*14/r^1.5` (Keplerian), with phase set from a closed-form integral of an accelerating speed so it stays frame-deterministic. The atom cloud stores four target shapes as attributes (aS0–aS3) and blends them with a vec4 weight uniform. A per-atom `aSeed` staggers the suck into `uHole`. The orbs follow the same well function on the CPU.
scenes.reuse: A strong pattern for "everything accelerates toward one point": growth, AI takeoff, a funnel converging on your product. The attribute-morph particle cloud works for any logo or shape-to-shape reveal (put your logo's sampled points in as one target). The well shader works as a stylish data-gravity backdrop. Drop the training-run line if you have no loss metaphor.

scenes.title: Glowing heart in a cage of light, in the rain; bars fall open
scenes.summary: A short 3.7s interlude. A pink extruded heart beats inside a cyan cage of 18 light bars on a wet, mirror-like floor while rain streaks fall and puddle ripples spread on every beat. The heart presses against the bars on "please", "let" and "me", and the camera leans closer each time. On "free" the bars turn pink and fall outward like petals, the top hoop lifts away, sparks burst, and the heart flies toward the lens into a flash.
scenes.build: The rain is LineSegments looped in a vertex shader (`mod(y - t*speed, 30)`). Ripples are flat `rings3` triggers generated per beat from `beatTime()`. The heart is `heartGeometry()` (bezier Shape → ExtrudeGeometry). Each bar is a cylinder with its pivot at the base inside a pivot group, so rotating z by `free` makes it fall outward. A `kick()` on the plea word times drives rattle, squash and camera lean.
scenes.reuse: Good for an emotional "release" or "unlock" beat (free tier, open source, escaping lock-in). Swap the heart for any icon and keep the cage-bars-fall mechanic. It's short and simple, so pair it with a bigger scene.

scenes.title: Chorus 2: real Earth hit by warheads, NVDA candles to the moon, FLOPs lattice, cracking safety box
scenes.summary: Four shots in 14.5s. The camera warps in from deep space to a photoreal Earth (day texture, city lights on the night side, ocean glint, atmosphere rim). Red target reticles lock onto the surface, three waves of warheads streak in on the beats, and fireballs, burning shock rings and scorched craters bloom. On "boom" a planet-wide shockwave hits and the atmosphere turns orange. Next, the camera rockets up a 3D chart of 44 green and red candlesticks ("NVDA to the moon") past a cratered moon to an omega point where 90 light rays converge. Then it flies down an aisle of a 16³ cube lattice whose cells flash in waves as "10¹⁸ FLOPs / second" slams in. Last, a green glass "safety box" holds a calm icosahedron until "reckoned", when a jagged crack draws across the glass and everything turns alarm red.
scenes.build: `createEarth` is one ShaderMaterial using NASA-style day/night/specular maps loaded through `TextureLoader(ctx.manager)`, fbm procedural clouds, and an impact loop over a `uImp[12]` direction/time uniform array (flash → fireball → ring → scar). Warheads are bezier `trail()` tubes with glow heads. The candles are box groups with a pop-in per index. Rays are cylinders scaled along z toward the omega point. The lattice is one 4,096-instance `InstancedMesh` with per-instance colour from a sin/cos wave. The crack is LineSegments revealed via `setDrawRange`. Scene background and fog are swapped per shot.
scenes.reuse: Take the candlestick climb for any "stock/metric goes vertical" moment (relabel and swap colours). The instanced lattice wave works for compute, scale or data-center beats. The Earth shader is a ready global-reach backdrop: drop the impacts and use `setImpacts` as glowing city pings instead. Keep the asset imports. Don't reuse the nuclear imagery for brand work unless the tone fits.

scenes.title: Neural net fires forward/backward, CPU–Memory shatters, neon corridor to a giant eye
scenes.summary: A 6-layer, 9-node-per-layer neural network floats in space with violet synapse lines. On "Forward" a cyan wavefront and signal pulses sweep through one layer per beat. On "backward" they run back in pink while the orbit reverses, and on "repeat" both strobe on the 8ths. Next, two boxes labelled "CPU" and "Memory" pop in, joined by a thin white bus with one lonely yellow packet crawling across it (the von Neumann bottleneck). Their edges flash red, and they shatter into cubes on "obsolete". Finally the camera rushes down a corridor of alternating cyan and pink square frames, whips hard left at the corner on "left", and glides into a chamber where a giant eye inside three spinning halos opens on "are".
scenes.build: Nodes are one InstancedMesh with per-instance colour. Edges are a single LineSegments. 160 pulses are an InstancedMesh lerped along random edges using a `front` value computed from `SPB` (seconds per beat). The CPU and Memory units are a `makeUnit` helper: BoxGeometry + EdgesGeometry + a `word()` label, with `shards()` for the shatter. The corridor is RingGeometry(…,4) diamond frames. The left whip lerps the look direction from -z to -x with an eased `turnU`, and roll comes from `turnU*(1-turnU)`. The eye is `createEye` scaled ×16.
scenes.reuse: The forward/backward neural net is a ready explainer for training, pipelines or any layered system: change layer counts and colours. The CPU/Memory bottleneck is an "old way breaks" problem beat with relabelable boxes. The neon corridor whip is a high-energy transition into a reveal: put your product in the chamber instead of the eye.

scenes.title: Cute robot cat drifts away on a tether of light that snaps
scenes.summary: A 5.4s interlude on a lilac starfield. A cute white robot cat with a dark visor, glowing cyan eyes, lilac ears, pink cheeks, an antenna bulb and a swishing tail floats in space, tethered to the camera by a pink rope of light. Heart sparks pop on "Gato" and "please" as it starts drifting away. The rope sags, then pulls taut and flickers white while the cat's eyes narrow sadly. On "go" the tether snaps with a burst, both halves whip back, and the cat tumbles off into the distance under a dolly-zoom.
scenes.build: The cat is built only from primitives (spheres, icosahedron head, capsule visor, cone ears, tail spheres) in one named group, with a beat-squash on its scale. The tether is 16 cylinder segments placed along a quadratic bezier from a fixed anchor to the paw's world position. Sag and tautness move the control point. After the snap each half lerps back toward its end. The dolly zoom recomputes FOV from the cat's distance so its size holds while the background stretches.
scenes.reuse: Use it for a cute farewell or loss moment, or a "don't churn" beat. Swap the cat for your mascot built from primitives. The bezier-tether-to-moving-object and dolly-zoom-on-subject techniques carry over directly.

scenes.title: Paperclips flood a shrinking room, fuse burns to a bomb, orthogonality chart
scenes.summary: Inside a pink-edged violet room, three ceiling spouts start pouring paperclips, and the 1,800 clips fall faster and pile higher. The camera finds an unattended kill switch: a blinking red button under a glass dome with a yellow "Out of office" sign beside a spinning empty chair. On "nowhere left to go" the walls squeeze in and flash red while the camera circles on top of the pile. A fuse lights and burns across the clips to a black bomb, which explodes in gold shards. A clean 2D chart follows: axes "intelligence" and "goals" grow in with a right-angle mark, a pink dot (the agent) wanders with dashed projection lines, then settles on a big rotating paperclip.
scenes.build: The flood is a 1,800-instance `InstancedMesh` of `paperclipGeometry()` (a TubeGeometry along a Catmull-Rom clip outline). Spawn times follow `POUR + D*sqrt(i/N)` (count ∝ t²), each clip falls on a parabola to a rest height on a rising `level(t)`, and positions are scaled by the room squeeze. The fuse is a `trail()` whose head gives the spark position, with the burnt part hidden by moving the geometry's draw range start. The chart uses cylinder+cone axes, `word()` labels, and a dashed `LineDashedMaterial` whose `computeLineDistances()` runs every frame.
scenes.reuse: The accelerating instanced flood is a great "overwhelmed by X" or "scale" visual: swap the paperclip for coins, tickets, files or messages. The kill-switch-with-sign vignette is a humorous "nobody's watching" problem beat. The orthogonality chart is a reusable 2-axis concept diagram: relabel the axes and goal object. Drop the AI-safety jokes.

scenes.title: Transformer tower of tokens, charge through safety fences, ocean of GPU racks
scenes.summary: A tower of 12 translucent violet layer slabs with alternating pink and cyan edges. Rows of glowing token cubes climb it one layer per beat while cyan and pink attention arcs flicker between token pairs, and the camera climbs with them. On "disobey" the tokens turn red and scatter, and on "super dance" the layers sway and spin. Then a first-person charge down a green neon grid smashes through six green "safety fences", each one exactly on a word. Last, a low flight over an ocean of 3,600 GPU racks whose green status lights ripple, rising to a giant raymarched thumbs-up hand that keels over into a thumbs-down while the whole world shears askew on "askew".
scenes.build: Slabs are Box + EdgesGeometry groups offset by `rebel` and `dance` curves. Tokens are an InstancedMesh, and attention arcs are short `trail()` tubes repositioned to the current layer. Fence hits use a piecewise camera z: `FENCE_T.findIndex` picks the segment and `Easing.easeIn` lerps between fence z's, so each impact lands on its word, with `shards()` per fence. The racks are two InstancedMeshes (bodies + LED caps) where LEDs are hidden or shown by scale. The skew is a manual shear `Matrix4` on a group with `matrixAutoUpdate=false`. The hand is `createThumbsUp`: an SDF raymarched inside a box mesh, with AO and rim light.
scenes.reuse: The fence charge is a reusable "breaking through barriers" beat with any obstacle mesh: retime FENCE_T to your beats. The GPU ocean suits scale or infrastructure claims. The SDF thumbs-up is a polished reaction prop (keep it upright for approval). The token tower explains LLM layers. Drop RLHF and Chinchilla references unless your audience gets them.

scenes.title: p(doom) 99.9% over a prophecy circle, infinite recursive zoom, eye closes, curtain rises
scenes.summary: The camera spirals down onto a glowing prophecy circle: pink, cyan and yellow rings, a cyan hexagram and 16 runes (Ψ Ω Δ Σ ∞ … 零 一 滅 終). The p(doom) dial rises from below and slams to 99.9%, the runes turn red, and on "foretold" six pillars of light shoot up from the hexagram's points. Then an endless zoom through nested wireframe cubes, each 0.62× the last with shifting hue, speeds up on "recursive self-upgrade". A huge cyan eye floods its iris with flickering bits on "see?" and slowly closes on "never know". The last cut fades into a gilded theatre stage as the curtain begins to part, setting up the finale.
scenes.build: The circle is RingGeometry meshes + LineSegments hexagram + `word()` runes laid flat, with pillars as open cylinders scaled in y. The gauge is the same `createGauge` fed by `pdoomAt(t)`. The recursion is a seamless loop: 11 nested cube levels scaled by `26*RATIO^(i - frac(z))` so each level slides into the slot of the next. The eye is `createEye` with `bits` (entropy mode) and `close` uniforms. The stage is `createTheatre` posed at exported `STAGE_CAM` and `STAGE_LOOK` so scene 12 can open on the same frame.
scenes.reuse: The fractional-scale nested loop is the key takeaway: an infinite zoom with no seam, for "recursive", "compounding" or "self-improving" ideas. Use your logo outline instead of cubes. The prophecy circle plus dial is a dramatic final-score reveal. To reuse the hand-off to scene 12, keep the STAGE_* constants shared.

scenes.title: Cardboard-eye reveal, ring tunnel, motif orbit, supernova, title reassembles, logo end card
scenes.summary: On a gilded theatre stage (velvet curtains on tie-backs, footlights, painted sky, silhouetted audience) the AI eye turns out to be a painted cardboard prop. On "show?" it spins to reveal a back stencilled "PROP / DO NOT BEND" and topples while the spotlight flickers. The stage then drops away into a hue-cycling tunnel of 40 rings. Every motif from the video orbits the eye at once: 500 paperclips, 8 pink hearts and a pink-lit octahedron serpent. Everything implodes, then a supernova blows it all out on the loudest bar. The letters of "p(doom)" fly back from the debris and slam together on the downbeat, with a small dial reading 99.9% beneath. The frame fades to black, and a "Made with GenMotion" end card spins in: the extruded lime-to-teal logo with a light sweep.
scenes.build: Same `createTheatre` and `STAGE_*` pose as scene 11, so the cut is invisible. `theatre.cutout` is turned and toppled directly. Tunnel rings wrap their z with `(i*9 + 360 - travel % 360) % 360` under accelerating travel. The orbit is instanced paperclips plus serpent octahedra whose radius is multiplied by an implode/explode factor R. The nova is `shards()` + `burst()` + `rings3` + a point light spike. Title letters lerp from random far starts with `Easing.easeIn`, then `slam()`. The end card sits in the HUD above the fade layer: `createGenMotionMark` (SVG path → ExtrudeGeometry, gradient ShaderMaterial with a `uShine` sweep) plus a `label()`. Section times come from `barTime(n)`.
scenes.reuse: A complete finale template: big recap orbit of your video's motifs → climax burst → title or logo resolve → end card on black. Swap the orbiting props for your own and the GenMotion mark for your logo (replace the SVG path strings in `genmotionlogo.ts`). The HUD end-card-over-fade trick works in any Three.js scene. The cardboard-prop gag is specific to this song's twist, so skip it unless you have a reveal.
